subject: ventures/sales-agent
professional: a B2B outbound / email-deliverability specialist (who also knows CAN-SPAM, PECR and CASL practice): first checks that the pre-send, list and auth checkers never give a false all-clear, then that unsubscribes are honoured without exception

evidence.correctness: Ran modules directly and recomputed independently. (1) Warm-up ramp: sendramp.plan({mailboxes:1,targetPerDay:40}) gave 19 days, first-week 95, schedule 10x3,15x3,...,40; a separate Python loop from the stated rule (start 10, +5 every 3 days, cap 40) gave the identical 19 days / 95. (2) 3 mailboxes, target 100: tool 16 days ending 90,90,90,100; Python gave the same. (3) SPF lookup counting against RFC 7208 section 4.6.4 (include, a, mx, ptr, exists, redirect count; ip4 and all do not): 'v=spf1 ip4:1.2.3.4 a mx -all' gives 2, three includes gives 3, matching a hand count. (4) DMARC pct=50 with p=reject warns per RFC 7489 semantics. Departures: SPF counts only top-level terms (includes are not resolved, so _spf.google.com counts as 1 although it nests more); disclosed in the code and warning text. presend postal-address check wrongly passes (see defects). Output wrong in one tested case, right in the rest.
evidence.completeness: Checked README claims by running: inbox agent, daily run, pre-send checker, sequence checker, warm-up planner, list cleaner, auth checker, call prep, follow-up, research, self-host all exist as modules with tests and (for the five checkers) HTML pages that import the modules (cold-email-warmup-planner.html imports ./sendramp.mjs). Test counts claimed in README match the files (presend 11, sequence 11, sendramp 6, listcheck 10, authcheck 13). No TODO/XXX in .mjs. Not run end to end: IMAP self-host against a live mailbox, Render/Fly one-click deploy, the model (BYOK) path.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/sales-agent && node --test '*.test.mjs': 215 tests, 215 pass, 0 fail, 1.6 s. Seeded mutations: authcheck.mjs 'lookups > 10' changed to '> 11' -> authcheck.test.mjs failed (1 of 13). sendramp.mjs step condition '=== 0' changed to '=== 1' -> sendramp.test.mjs failed (1 of 6). Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Tests are boundary-sensitive in these modules. Gap: the presend postal-address regex false pass has no test.
evidence.craft: Read authcheck.mjs, sendramp.mjs, listcheck.mjs, presend.mjs in full; README, llms.txt. Small pure modules, input validation in plan() (need()), clear comments with limits, no network. Defects: presend POSTAL regex ends with \b\d{5}(-\d{4})?\b so any 5-digit number satisfies it; presend OPT_OUT matches the word 'unsubscribe' anywhere (e.g. 'reduce unsubscribe rates'); DISPOSABLE list is 15 domains and TYPOS a fixed map; DKIM key size inferred from base64 length only (4096-bit reports 2048). Hard-coded regime tables are plain data, acceptable.
evidence.claims: README/llms.txt claims checked against files: 'no send path, a test fails if one appears' -> test present in suite and passes; eval numbers (70% / 66% / 83% on fresh sets) are labelled tuned vs fresh, with limits, which is unusually honest; presend regimes marked 'from memory, statute unread'. Unbacked or stale: llms.txt and sitemap link 7 times to duncan-haywood.github.io and 0 times to marisstella.app although CLAUDE.md says GitHub Pages now only redirects; README says the presend checker has '10 tests' in one paragraph and 11 in the next; the checker says a clean result is not delivery, but 'CAN-SPAM requires ... postal address' check can be satisfied by a number, so 'lists a missing postal address' is overstated.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a small outbound team: sort replies, honour opt-outs, pre-check an email, clean a list, check SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, plan a ramp. Each step produced a usable answer from pasted text with no signup. Limits a user hits: authentication checks are offline (cannot resolve includes or fetch records), list cleaning cannot verify mailboxes, replies tested mainly on agent-written text.
evidence.domain: Compared against RFC 7208/7489/6376, CAN-SPAM (16 CFR 316), Google/Yahoo 2024 bulk-sender rules. Sound: opt-out and suppression-first design, drafts only, 0.1%/0.3% complaint thresholds, separate sending domain advice. Departures a deliverability specialist would flag: SPF nested lookups and void-lookup limit not evaluated; DMARC alignment/policy not tested against SPF/DKIM domains; no List-Unsubscribe / one-click RFC 8058 check in presend although the ramp text mentions it; disposable list tiny; the ramp's 40/day cap is a rule of thumb, stated as such.

defects.what: Postal-address check passes on any bare 5-digit number (probe: body 'we work with 20000 firms' produced no postal-address error for country US), so CAN-SPAM missing-address errors are silently skipped
Opt-out check passes if the word 'unsubscribe' (or 'opt out') appears anywhere in the body, not as an instruction to the reader
SPF lookup count ignores nested includes, so a record such as three provider includes reports 3 lookups; real count can exceed 10 and cause permerror (disclosed, but no resolve option)
Disposable-domain set holds only 15 domains; guerrillamail.info style variants return 'send' (probe)
llms.txt and sitemap point to the retired github.io host, not marisstella.app

verdict: A well-tested, honest flagship: 215 of 215 tests pass, two seeded mutations were both caught, ramp and SPF counts recompute exactly, and the README labels tuned versus fresh accuracy. It falls short of a deliverability or compliance specialist's sign-off because the pre-send checker can give a false all-clear on the two things CAN-SPAM turns on (postal address, opt-out), the SPF check is offline-only, and llms.txt links the retired host. Correctness is 3 only on the modules probed; the reply-classifier accuracy rests on agent-written text and was not re-measured here.
